expected.note: IRS computation (85% of $26,802 SSDI) which petitioner did not challenge; court granted summary judgment for respondent on the deficiency; 2023/2024 repayments do not reduce 2022 benefits under 86(d)(2)(A)
expected.snippet: The IRS calculated that $22,782—i.e., 85% of the $26,802 of SSDI benefits petitioner received during 2022—was includible in his gross income

expected.note: sustained in full (decision for respondent with respect to the deficiency); includes petitioner's conceded $1,454 unreported retirement income
expected.snippet: An appropriate order and decision will be entered for respondent with respect to the deficiency and for petitioner with respect to the penalty.
In his Motion respondent concedes the accuracy-related penalty.

issues_outside_coverage: Claim-of-right doctrine (North American Oil) does not exclude benefits later repaid
Repayments in later years (2023/2024) cannot be considered in the 2022 deficiency case; relief, if any, belongs to the repayment year (annual accounting, sec. 451(a))
decisive_judgment_findings: Petitioner did not dispute receiving $26,802 of SSDI benefits in 2022 and did not challenge the mechanics of the section 86 computation
No repayment to SSA was made during 2022; all repayments were in 2023 and 2024
Petitioner received the benefits under a claim of right (he applied and SSA affirmed entitlement; reversal came only in 2023)
